text:
maria: FYI proposing an RBAC change for the keystore event stream and a short rollout plan. need quick eyes because this touches KMS key usage and our SAST gating.
kevin: can you summarize the risk? is this only read-only for the audit consumer or wider perms? :thinking_face:
maria: it's a scoped read-only consumer role for the new event-forwarder service. downside: if misconfigured we could leak keystore metadata (not keys) to downstream pipelines. not catastrophic but sensitive.
olivia: tagging audit concerns — are we streaming any PII or secret material? need to confirm SAST/DAST findings on code that serializes events.
maria: no PII, no plaintext key material. but SCA flagged a serializer pattern in the forwarder that could include env-bytes if env var injection happens. GH #452 shows the exact lines.
security-bot: Alert: SAST high-severity rule 'config-injection' triggered in repo redwood/forwarder at src/serializer.go:78. See https://scans.internal/sast/452
kevin: ok, plan of action?
maria: propose 3-phase:
  1) short-term: apply RBAC read-only role with attribute-based filter so consumer only sees event.headers and non-secret payloads. deploy in canary region.
  2) mid-term: patch serializer to explicitly redact env-sourced bits and add unit tests + SAST suppression review.
  3) long-term: add a pre-merge SAST gate and a binary DAST smoke test in staging that validates no secret patterns are emitted in event stream.
kevin: sounds reasonable. for (1) can we do an audit-log smoke test to validate no secret fields flow? how do we query logs for a canary run?
olivia: use the audit log query below (GCP example). run after canary deploy and check for any 'secret' token patterns.

# gcloud logging read "resource.type=gae_app AND jsonPayload.stream=\"keystore-events\"" --limit 100 --project=redwood-canary
# then pipe to jq to scan keys
gcloud logging read "..." | jq -r '.jsonPayload | @json' | grep -E "(secret|password|key)"

maria: also add an application-level redaction test in the forwarder e2e: payloads with env-vars should assert redacted==true.
devex: I'll update the pre-merge pipeline template to add the SAST check as required and include a comment template for suppression requests. also will add a checklist step for keystore-related changes: `RBAC impact, KMS decrypt test, audit log smoke`.
oncall: if anything floods logs or shows a secret leak, rollback plan is immediate: revoke the consumer role, pause forwarder, open INC-1234, and run forensic export of last 1k events. owners: @kevin (rollback) and @maria (postmortem + remediation).
kevin: i'll take ownership of the canary deploy and the rollback play. will coordinate with oncall for monitoring.
maria: thanks. olivia, can you do the SAST suppression review once kevin/link PR lands? cc @devex for pipeline update timeline.
olivia: yep, will review. quick checklist for reviewers: 1) evidence in unit tests that redaction works, 2) audit-log query output attached to PR, 3) minimal RBAC policy diff.
security-bot: Note: Remember to attach KMS audit logs (keyring access) for post-deploy verification. KMS audit retention is 90 days.
maria: I'll link a short runbook in the PR: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/keystore-streaming-rbac
kevin: rough ETA for canary deploy: today + 4 hours. will post results here.
maria: :thumbsup: closing loop — if we see anything odd after 30m of canary traffic we roll back. otherwise progress to mid-term patch and gating.
oncall: added INC-1234 and assigned alert contact. will monitor dashboards (keystore-errors, audit-exceptions). :lock:
kevin: deployed canary, running audit query now, will paste output in 15m.
maria: thanks, everyone. follow-ups: devex will update pipeline, olivia will sign off SAST suppression (if any), kevin runs canary + rollback if needed.
